name: Generative and Style-based Models
text:
# Generative and Style-based Models

Also called: 3D-aware generative radiance fields, NeRF-GAN hybrids

## Overview
This family extends parametric radiance fields from deterministic scene reconstruction to probabilistic 3D-aware image synthesis. It solves the problem of generating novel, high-quality 3D-consistent views from limited data (e.g., single images or noise) by replacing or augmenting photometric reconstruction losses with generative objectives, such as adversarial training or score distillation from pre-trained diffusion models [S1]. Unlike [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) which optimizes a single scene representation for a fixed dataset, these methods generate diverse 3D structures or latent codes, enabling applications in 3D-aware image generation where camera positions may be unavailable or where explicit conditioning is required [S1].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism remains the parametric function $F_\Theta$ that maps a 3D position $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and a viewing direction $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ to a volume density $\sigma \in \mathbb{R}$ and an RGB color $\mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^3$. This function is implemented as one or more neural networks, typically utilizing [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$ to map raw coordinates to a higher-dimensional space using sinusoidal functions at increasing frequencies [Parent].

**Rendering Integration:**
During training, rays are sampled at points $\mathbf{x}_i$ along the ray. The networks predict $\sigma_i$ and $\mathbf{c}_i$. The pixel color $C(\mathbf{r})$ is computed via volumetric rendering:
$$
C(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^N T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{c}_i, \quad \text{where } \alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i), \quad T_i = \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j)
$$
and $\delta_i$ is the distance between samples [Parent].

**Input Representation:**
Raw coordinates are rarely used directly. They are mapped to a higher-dimensional space using positional encoding $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$. For a coordinate $\mathbf{x}$, the encoding includes the original value and sinusoidal functions at increasing frequencies:
$$
\gamma(\mathbf{x}) = (\sin(2^0 \pi \mathbf{x}), \cos(2^0 \pi \mathbf{x}), \dots, \sin(2^{L-1} \pi \mathbf{x}), \cos(2^{L-1} \pi \mathbf{x}))
$$
where $L$ is the number of frequency bands [Parent].

## Subtopics

### [HyperNeRFGAN](8765-hypernerfgan.md)
A GAN-based approach that uses a hypernetwork to generate the weights of a simplified [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) from a Gaussian noise vector. It removes viewing directions from the input, assuming view-independent appearance, and replaces deterministic optimization with a generative adversarial objective. Choose this when camera poses are unavailable or for 3D-aware generation without explicit conditioning.

### [Latent-NeRF](9110-latent-nerf.md)
Integrates pre-trained latent diffusion models by optimizing the NeRF to produce latent features that align with a diffusion prior via score distillation. It replaces standard [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md) with perceptual consistency from the diffusion model. Choose this for high-quality novel view synthesis from limited inputs (single image/text) where perceptual quality is prioritized over exact photometric reconstruction.

### StyleNeRF
**Definition:** A 3D-aware generative model that merges 3D scene representation with style-based generative models [S1].
**Steps:** Uses NeRF to generate low-resolution feature maps and samples them to high resolution to avoid super-computation volume rendering. Applies [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) to improve 3D consistency [S1].

## Background
The intersection of NeRF and GANs began with Schwarz et al. (2020) proposing [GRAF](#8539-graf.md), which introduced a discriminator to control shape and appearance, though limited to single-object scenes [S1]. Niemeyer et al. (2021) proposed [GIRAFFE](#11360-giraffe.md), separating object shape, appearance, and background in a compositional generative neural feature field [S1]. Chan et al. (2021) introduced [pi-GAN](#10298-pi-gan.md), using periodic activation functions for high-quality 3D-aware image synthesis, though requiring large data for complex scenes [S1]. Gu et al. (2022) proposed StyleNeRF, merging 3D scene representation with style-based generation to address view-conditioning and noise injection issues [S1]. These methods generally lack the scalability of standard NeRF for complex, realistic scenes [S1].
